subject: maths
question: A runs at a speed that is (11)/(9) times the speed of B. If B is allowed to have a head start such that B beats A by (1)/(3) of the length of the race, what part of the length of the race has been given as head start to B over A? [Note: Consider A and B to start running at the same time.]
solution:
**Given**

A's speed = 11/9 times B's speed

B beats A by 1/3 of the length of the race

**Calculation:**

The ratio of speed of A and B is 11 : 9

Let the total race be 90 units.

Let the head start given by B to A is x.

Total distance covered by A = 60 units which is 1/3 less of total distance.

Total distance covered by B = 90 - x

According to the question:

⇒ 60/11 = (90 - x)/9

⇒ 11x = 450

⇒ x = 450/11

The part is = 450/(11 × 90) = 5/11

**Therefore, the part of the length of the race that has been given as a head start to B over A is 5/11.**
